summary: Phase 7 (Stripe/Boost — Lane B) tested end-to-end. Backend: 13/13 pytest cases pass covering seeded tiers, admin CRUD (create/edit/hide/deactivate/delete), 400 on missing duration/until_sold, global feature toggle, hidden-vs-visible visibility (admin vs seller /boost/options), unauth denial, owner-only boost checkout returning valid https://checkout.stripe.com URL + session_id, free-path ($0 boost) instantly setting featured=true and surfacing in /listings?featured=true, unauthenticated GET /payments/status/{session_id} returning kind=boost/pending, and Lane A separation (buy-now creates no Stripe session). Frontend: Admin /admin renders boost-admin-panel with 3 seeded rows and boost-feature-toggle plus create form. Sell /sell wizard steps 1→2→3 all work; boost tiers render (4 items incl. free), listing summary values update ($240 asking / $0 fee / $0→$9→$0 boost / total tracks), review-total matches, and Publish without featuring navigates to /listing/{id}.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~1988 lines — recommend splitting boost/payments into a separate module (routers/boosts.py) for maintainability; not blocking.
boost_checkout uses require_verified but does not re-validate that the listing is in 'live' status; a seller could theoretically boost a draft/sold listing. Consider adding a status check.

_apply_boost overwrites featured/featured_until unconditionally — if a longer 'Until Sold' boost is already active, buying a 3-day boost afterward would shorten the featured window. Consider preserving the longer of the two.

/api/payments/status/{session_id} is unauthenticated by design; anyone knowing a session_id can trigger stripe.Session.retrieve and fulfillment. Low risk (session_ids are unguessable) but worth documenting.
